_comment: Hierarchical AllToAll on the DUAL-PLANE rail-optimized 256-GPU cluster (300 fine nodes -> 44 coarse: 32 host cells + 8 leaves + 4 spines, planes fully isolated). Topology comes from teccl/topologies/topology-dsl-frontend/examples/rail_optimized_256gpu_dual_plane.topo; the path is relative to the repo root, i.e. to the directory `teccl solve` runs from. A/B partner of rail_optimized_256gpu_hierarchical_alltoall.json: same 32x8 GPUs, same switch count, same NVSwitch host fabric -- the difference is the fabric cut, 2x400 Gbps per GPU into a 2:1 tapered spine tier here versus one 400 Gbps rail into a non-blocking tier there.
_expected: At chunk_size = 1 GB per (src,dst) GPU pair, each GPU ships 248 GB across the host boundary (255 peers - 7 host-mates on the NVSwitch), split over its two 400 Gbps plane rails = 100 GB/s of egress, so the GPU port alone would finish in 2.48 s. It is NOT the binding cut: the .topo file was retuned to 2:1 oversubscription (leaf-spine edges are now 16 x 400 Gbps = 6400 Gbps, down from 32 x 400), and the SPINE CUT now binds. Per plane-A leaf l: the 64 GPUs on rails l and l+4 each put 124 GB into that plane, of which 31 GB turns around on the leaf (the 62 cross-host same-leaf peers, halved per plane), leaving 93 GB x 64 = 5952 GB of up-traffic against 2 x 800 = 1600 GB/s of uplink = 3.72 s. So T* >= 3.72 s = 3 pinned epochs -- 1.5x the GPU-port bound, which is the 2:1 taper showing up exactly where the topology header says it should. Compare against the single-plane run: that one is rail-bound at 4.96 s, so a tapered dual plane still wins here, just by less than its 2x of GPU port bandwidth would suggest.
_epoch_note: epoch_duration is PINNED to 1.24 s at the ROOT level only (list form: [USER_INPUT, FASTEST_LINK] / [1.24, -1]; depths past the end of a list take its last entry, so every level below the coarse LP keeps deriving its own epoch). 1.24 s makes the 3.72 s bound land on an integer epoch count (3) with nothing lost to the final ceiling, and is the SAME quantum the single-plane sibling pins, so the two runs are comparable epoch for epoch. FASTEST_LINK at the root would size the epoch off the coarse leaf-spine link, 2048 GB (a host's whole send buffer, the coarse chunk) / 800 GB/s = 2.56 s, which ceilings 3.72 s up to 5.12 s -- a 38% quantization loss, and a loss that grew when the fabric was tapered (at the old 12800 Gbps edges the derived epoch was 1.28 s, and the earlier 2.56 s answer in Schedules/rail_dp_alltoall_epochs_ring_coarse.json was cheap only by luck). The pin is legal because the root is solved by a real formulation (the LP answers a shorter epoch with more epochs); the >= fastest-link floor in hierarchy/solve.level_epoch_duration only guards the closed-form levels, which is why they are left on FASTEST_LINK.
